result:
No. The server has no logout flow that touches the FCM token. A search of `src/` for "logout" (case-insensitive) finds nothing outside the FCM unregister code. `auth.service.ts` only reads the token (`getDeviceTokenByUserId` at `src/auth/auth.service.ts:230,273,501`) and never removes it.

Three things deactivate a token today. All of them soft-delete by setting `isActive=false` and `deletedAt`, not by removing the row:

1. **Explicit call from the client.** `DELETE /fcm/unregister-token/:deviceId` (`src/fcm/fcm.controller.ts:51-64`) calls `FcmService.unregisterDeviceToken` (`src/fcm/fcm.service.ts:127-140`). It deactivates the row matching `userId` and `deviceId`. The app would have to call this on logout, and nothing on the server enforces that.
2. **Next registration.** `registerDeviceToken` (`src/fcm/fcm.service.ts:97-103`) calls `unregisterAllDeviceTokens` (`:146-151`) if the user already has any row. That deactivates all of that user's tokens before it saves the new one. So only the next login or registration on any device cleans up the old token.
3. **Nothing else.** I didn't look for a cleanup job or for handling of invalid-token errors from FCM at send time.

Until one of those happens, the old token stays `isActive=true`. `getUserDeviceToken` (`src/fcm/fcm.service.ts:158-164`) returns any active row for the user, so a logged-out device can still receive pushes.
